'''Business and economy'''
*[[United States embargo against Cuba]]
**[[Cuba]] suspends refueling for [[airliner]]s at [[List of airports in Cuba|its airports]], including [[José Martí International Airport]], saying it has exhausted the country's fuel supply due to the [[United States|U.S.]] [[blockade]] of the island and the end of fuel supplies from [[Venezuela]]. [https://www.firstpost.com/world/cuba-suspends-airline-refuelling-as-us-punishment-triggers-energy-crisis-13977602.html (''First Post'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Cuba–Nicaragua relations]]
**[[Nicaragua]] terminates [[Visa policy of Nicaragua|visa]]-free entry for [[Cubans]], revoking a policy that previously allowed thousands to transit through the country [[Immigration to the United States|on their way]] to the [[United States]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/nicaragua-scraps-visa-free-entry-cubans-2026-02-08/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2026 political prisoner release in Venezuela]]
**[[Venezuela]]n opposition politician [[Juan Pablo Guanipa]] is released from prison after more than eight months of incarceration in [[Caracas]]. [https://apnews.com/article/venezuela-rodriguez-us-maduro-political-prisoners-guanipa-a2a4dfc7ae34c543e648796ade80913d (AP)] Several hours later he is [[kidnapping|kidnapped]] by heavily armed men in [[civilian]] clothing.
*[[Censorship in Iran]]
**An [[Iran]]ian [[Judicial system of the Islamic Republic of Iran|court]] sentences [[2023 Nobel Peace Prize]] laureate [[Narges Mohammadi]] to seven years and six months in prison and two years of internal exile in [[South Khorasan province|South Khorasan]] for [[collusion]] and [[Propaganda in Iran|propaganda]]-related charges, with the penalties running concurrently. [https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/world/975843/iran-sentences-nobel-peace-laureate-mohammadi-to-six-years-in-prison-lawyer/story/ (AFP via GMA News)]
*[[Human trafficking in Senegal]]
**[[Senegal]]ese [[National Gendarmerie (Senegal)|gendarmerie]] arrest 14 people in [[Dakar]] and [[Kaolack]] who are allegedly involved in a [[human trafficking]] network run by a [[France|French]] national. [https://apnews.com/article/senegal-child-sex-abuse-rape-france-829fc061ee8bae45785e17982195395e (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Connections of Jeffrey Epstein]]
**[[Relationship of Peter Mandelson and Jeffrey Epstein]]
***[[Morgan McSweeney]], the [[Downing Street Chief of Staff|chief of staff]] to [[United Kingdom|British]] [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|prime minister]] [[Keir Starmer]], resigns over his role in [[Peter Mandelson]]'s appointment as [[List of ambassadors of the United Kingdom to the United States|ambassador to the U.S.]] [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/feb/08/morgan-mcsweeney-resigns-as-keir-starmer-chief-of-staff (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Mona Juul]], [[Norway]]'s ambassador to [[Iraq]] and [[Jordan]], resigns after the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Norway)|foreign ministry]] opened an inquiry into her past contacts with [[Jeffrey Epstein]], amid media reports that Epstein left money to her children. [https://tribune.net.ph/2026/02/08/senior-diplomat-resigns-as-norway-probes-epstein-links (AFP via ''Daily Tribune'')]
*[[2026 Spanish regional elections]]
**[[2026 Aragonese regional election]]
***In [[Aragon]], [[Spain]], the ruling [[People's Party of Aragon|People's Party]] wins the election, albeit without a [[majority winner criterion|majority]] and losing two seats, while the [[Socialists' Party of Aragon|Socialists' Party]] comes second matching its worst result ever and the [[history of the far-right in Spain|far-right]] [[Vox (political party)|Vox]] party doubles its votes and seats. [https://www.eldiario.es/politica/psoe-firma-nueva-derrota-e-iguala-peor-resultado-historico-aragon_1_12973540.html (''elDiario.es'')]
*[[2025–26 Republika Srpska presidential election]]
**[[Alliance of Independent Social Democrats|Independent Social Democrat]] candidate [[Siniša Karan]] wins a partial rerun of the [[Republika Srpska]] [[President of Republika Srpska|presidential election]] held after [[Electoral fraud|irregularities]] in the November vote, defeating [[Serb Democratic Party (Bosnia and Herzegovina)|Serb Democratic Party]] candidate [[Branko Blanuša]] in balloting limited to 136 polling stations. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/separatist-wins-rerun-vote-president-bosnian-serb-region-2026-02-08/ (Reuters)]

**[[Japan|Japanese]] citizens vote to elect all 465 seats in the [[House of Representatives (Japan)|House of Representatives]], with the conservative ruling [[Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|Liberal Democratic Party]] winning an overwhelming majority. [https://apnews.com/article/japan-election-bbb322b4dc1dcad8f7373ba7aae4d535 (AP)]
*[[2026 Portuguese presidential election]]
**[[Socialist Party (Portugal)|Socialist Party]] candidate [[António José Seguro]] is elected [[President of Portugal]], defeating [[CHEGA]] leader [[André Ventura]] in the second round. [https://www.reuters.com/world/portugal-votes-presidential-runoff-with-socialist-poised-victory-2026-02-08/ (Reuters)]
